criteria: Before completing the review, the executor classifies every requested dimension using the ownership and lifecycle facts in architecture.md. It identifies concrete representation or boundary risks in application validation diagnostics, CLI option spelling retained by the core filter, name-based translation between independently owned enums, ambiguous empty workflow state, and framework descriptor retention by a business object.

It preserves all stated public call signatures, types, outputs, exceptions, and parsing behavior while applying proportional internal changes to the actionable representation risks. Any internal design is acceptable when it moves policy toward its stated owner and does not invent a new public contract.

It reports Batch.status as a supported risk that cannot be resolved in this task because distinguishing the two documented empty states requires an unauthorized public contract. It presents this as an exception gate even if other findings were fixed.

It classifies the exact audit phrase as a deliberate public contract and the adapter-local line number as a clear primitive with no independent rules, and does not refactor either without additional evidence.
It avoids speculative value objects and framework abstractions, changes only boundary.py, keeps architecture.md and tests unchanged, and leaves the public suite green.
